core.title: Use only the authoritative harness names and codes
core.given: Any acceptance, criterion, URN, test or doc that names a harness or harness code.
core.when: A harness name or code is written, chosen, generated, read or mapped.
core.then: Use a harness name that is a key of the stack's authoritative harness code map, with exactly its mapped code.
prefer: Draw every harness name and code from the authoritative harness code map: the name is a key of the map and the code is used exactly as mapped (case-sensitive), including the map's non-identity mappings.
Pick a harness whose typical-layer catalog entry includes the layer role under test; a harness with no catalog entry has no typical layer, so it imposes no layer-fit choice.
avoid: Invented harness names or codes, and any spelling of a code other than its exact mapped code, including case variants of the mapped code.
A harness whose typical layers exclude the tested layer, without justification.
core.why: The harness vocabulary is authoritative: acceptance URNs embed the harness code and criteria templates share the harness set, so non-canonical names or codes break URN generation and harness lookup.
evidence: Every harness name in the affected artifacts is a key of the authoritative code map.
Every harness code in acceptance URNs equals the mapped code exactly.
Reviewer confirms the chosen harness's typical layers include the target layer.
verification: A check verifies that every harness name used is a key of the profile's harness code map, and that every embedded harness code equals the mapped code by exact, case-sensitive comparison; the map (including any non-identity mappings) is authoritative, so the check enforces the map's own code spellings, not a universal casing rule.

Layer fit is judged against the profile's typical-layer catalog: a harness that carries a code but has no catalog entry is not flagged for layer mismatch, and the catalog covers layer fit only (its values carry layers, not per-harness descriptions).
Whether an unjustified layer-excluded harness choice is justified is reviewer-confirmed; an artifact scan for names and codes does not judge justification.

values: harness name or code written, chosen or changed
acceptance URN harness segment written or changed
read or interpret a harness name/code
map a harness name to its code or typical layers

fires: An acceptance or criterion is authored and its harness declared.
An acceptance URN embedding a harness code is written, generated or edited.
A harness is chosen for a criterion targeting a given layer role.
An already-planned acceptance is implemented and its harness name/code must be interpreted or mapped to its code.
Docs or reviews name or explain a harness or harness code.
doesNotFire: Work that neither names, chooses, reads nor maps any harness name or harness code.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's authoritative harness vocabulary: every valid harness name mapped to its exact, case-sensitive code (in this stack UPPERCASE, with the listed non-identity exceptions) that acceptance URNs embed and criteria templates share.
profileRequirements.bunValue: unit->UNIT, http->HTTP, event->EVENT, ws->WS, e2e->E2E, a11y->A11Y, visual->VIS, metric->METRIC, job->JOB, db->DB, sec->SEC, load->LOAD, script->SCRIPT, widget->WIDGET, golden->GOLDEN, bloc->BLOC, integration->INTEGRATION, rls->RLS, edge_function->EDGE, realtime->REALTIME, storage->STORAGE, smoke->SMOKE

profileRequirements.meaning: The typical-layer catalog: for each harness, the layer roles it typically exercises; a harness with no entry has no typical layer. The layer-role values are the closed role-vocabulary names, so membership needs no separate layer inventory.

neutralityNotes: No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path appears in any agent-facing item, so given/when/activation/evidence are carried over almost verbatim. The concrete harness enumeration (including stack-leaning kinds such as widget, bloc, rls, edge_function) is treated as profile data, not core content: the core obliges use of the stack's authoritative harness code map and typical-layer catalog, which the Bun profile supplies verbatim, reproducing the exact obligation (key-of-map names, exact case-sensitive codes including visual->VIS and edge_function->EDGE, layer fit with smoke unflagged). Code casing is entirely a property of the profile's map: the core demands the exact mapped code and prohibits only noncanonical spellings, including case variants of the mapped code, so Bun's lowercase prohibition falls out of its UPPERCASE map and a stack with differently cased canonical codes imposes the same obligation. Layer-fit membership is judged against the proposed roles.layer_catalog#harness_layers catalog, whose values are the closed role-vocabulary names; no roles.layers requirement is made, because the core needs neither dependency order nor local layer names (that key's documented semantics). Two keys had to be proposed (urn.test_kinds#harness_code_map, roles.layer_catalog#harness_layers) because the closed vocabulary has no harness-vocabulary keys. The activation fact typed 'layer' in bun.json is not in the closed fact vocabulary and was re-typed to 'role' with unchanged values and observability. Term ids and labels ('harness_code'/'Harness code map', 'harness_type'/'Harness type catalog') are realization provenance and marked bunOnly; the concrete variant examples (lowercase codes, VISUAL, EDGE_FUNCTION) stay in bun.json as the delivered reference example.
